dedupe_keys.name: carb landfill gas tool first order decay landfill methane and heat input model

description: The Landfill Gas Tool is a spreadsheet model that estimates how much landfill gas a municipal solid waste landfill produces over time, using the first-order decay method of the 2006 Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change guidelines. The California Air Resources Board built it to help landfill owners and operators comply with California's landfill methane regulation. For a landfill without a gas collection system it calculates the heat input capacity in million British thermal units per hour required under section 95471(b)(1); for landfills with collection and control systems it estimates the expected gas flow rate. Users enter annual waste acceptance by waste type, opening and closing years, and climate-related decay parameters. It is usable for any landfill, though its defaults and compliance thresholds follow California rules, and the Excel workbook, last updated on 24 September 2021, is free to download from the board's website. Caveats: first-order decay results carry large uncertainty, the tool is designed for regulatory screening, not engineering design, and it does not model gas migration or collection efficiency in detail. Simulation uses: estimating methane generation and energy potential at landfills for climate adaptation and mitigation planning, and checking whether sites need gas control. Related records: EPA's LandGEM (model-landgem) is the federal counterpart, the EPA LMOP landfill database (data-epa-lmop-landfill-and-project-database) lists landfill gas projects, and the machine-readable IPCC 2006 waste emission factors (data-waste-treatment-disposal-emission-factors-ipcc-2006-vol-5-machine-readable-p02950) provide inputs.
